positivePaths: reconnect after caller writes inline-block: re-asserted to "block" (jsdom + browser — browser now sets the conflicting value before reconnect)

ATTR-021.browserTest: ATTR-021: close() sets data-motion="closing" during exit then removes it
ATTR-021.negativeBrowserTest: ATTR-021: opening does not carry data-motion="closing" (negative)
ATTR-021.observable: public close() sets data-motion="closing" on the popup synchronously; the real computed dropdownExit animation (160ms) keeps the panel display:block during exit; once the animation completes (animationend / fallback timer) data-motion is removed and display becomes none
positivePaths: close() -> data-motion="closing" (captured synchronously in the close() turn)
after exit completes -> data-motion removed and display none (polled)
ATTR-021.determinism: Uses the real default --select-dropdown-exit-animation (dropdownExit 160ms) resolved by Chromium; no private method, no fixed sleeps — observed via public close() + getComputedStyle-derived animation, asserted with expect.poll for removal
ATTR-021.whyBrowserOnly: jsdom does not resolve stylesheet-derived animation-name -> computed duration 0 -> data-motion is set then immediately cleared (never observable at rest)

ATTR-022.jsdomTest: ATTR-022: multi-select defaults to data-multi-scroll-mode="wrap" and data-drag-scroll="false"
ATTR-022.observable: attributes reflect selection.mode + multiSelectDisplay.mode/.dragScroll on the input container

ATTR-023.browserTest: ATTR-023: no data-virtual-spacer renders on the public surface for a large list (gap)
ATTR-023.gap: data-virtual-spacer is NOT reachable through the public surface in the current build. The guarded virtualizer that emits spacers (_createGuardedSpacer) is created only inside _ensureGuardedVirtualizer; every entered caller requires _guardedVirtualizer/_guardedVirtualizationRequested to already be established. The only setter of _guardedVirtualizationRequested=true is the private _updateGuardedVirtualWindow, which has NO callers in src; the existing accepted spacer tests (enhanced-select-virtualization-integration.spec.ts, selected-options-virtualization.spec.ts) drive it via the private helper setGuardedWindow -> _updateGuardedVirtualWindow. No public config/method (incl. dataLoading.protocol='acknowledged' + startDataLoading, or virtualize:true) establishes the window. A 2000-item virtualizable list renders options with 0 spacers in real Chromium. NEGATIVE-ONLY coverage recorded: the browser test asserts safe, deterministic absence rather than positive spacer behavior. Remains Diagnostic (private/test-seam reachable only), analogous to PART-009's documented gap; deferred, not forced with a private stub.
negativePaths: BOUNDED to 2,000 items + virtualize:true via public methods: at the settled completed-render checkpoint (all 2,000 [part="option"] rendered) there are 0 [data-virtual-spacer]; a subsequent options scroll cycle keeps the render complete and still 0 spacers
ATTR-023.synchronization: No arbitrary sleep: synchronized on the observable completed-render state (expect.poll until exactly BIG.length options render), then a public scroll gesture followed by re-synchronization on the same completed-render state before reading spacer count. Bounded claim: absence at this tested public configuration/checkpoint, not universal unreachability.

corrections.finding: Arbitrary page.waitForTimeout(50) in the ATTR-023 test; AC-4 requires deterministic tests without arbitrary delays, and a 50ms probe does not establish a settled lifecycle.
corrections.resolution: Removed the fixed wait. The test now synchronizes on the observable completed-render state (expect.poll until exactly 2,000 [part="option"] render), reads spacers, drives a public scroll cycle, re-synchronizes on the same completed-render state, and re-asserts 0 spacers. Claim explicitly bounded to the tested 2,000-item + virtualize:true configuration and checkpoint (no universal-unreachability claim).

corrections.finding: The browser ATTR-013 test reconnected without first writing a conflicting caller display, so it only showed display stays 'block', not that Chromium overwrites a conflicting caller value (jsdom proved the override).
corrections.resolution: Browser test now sets a conflicting inline display ('inline-block') before reconnect and asserts it is overwritten back to 'block' after reconnection — the override is proven in Chromium as well as jsdom. Attribution updated to jsdom + browser-confirmed override.
